claims.quote: Barbiturates are contraindicated in patients with known barbiturate sensitivity.

claims.text: manifest or latent porphyria, severe respiratory distress with dyspnea or obstruction;
claims.quote: Barbiturates are also contraindicated in patients with a history of manifest or latent porphyria, marked impairment of liver functions or with severe respiratory distress where dyspnea or obstruction is evident.
Intraarterial administration is contraindicated. Its consequences vary from transient pain to gangrene.

claims.text: Too-rapid IV: severe respiratory depression, apnea, laryngospasm, hypertension or vasodilation with a fall in BP.
claims.quote: Too rapid administration may cause severe respiratory depression, apnea, laryngospasm, hypertension or vasodilation with fall in blood pressure.

claims.text: Other CNS depressants (eg, alcohol, narcotics, tranquilizers, antihistamines): additive CNS depression.
claims.quote: Concurrent use of the barbiturates with other CNS depressants (e.g., alcohol, narcotics, tranquilizers and antihistamines) may result in additional CNS depressant effects.

claims.text: Overdose: CNS and respiratory depression (can progress to Cheyne-Stokes respiration), areflexia, slightly constricted pupils (paralytic dilation possible in severe poisoning), oliguria, tachycardia, hypotension, low body temperature, coma.
claims.quote: Acute overdosage with barbiturates is manifested by CNS and respiratory depression which may progress to Cheyne-Stokes respiration, areflexia, constriction of the pupils to a slight degree (though in severe poisoning, they may show paralytic dilation), oliguria, tachycardia, hypotension, lowered body temperature and coma.
